notes: Temporary diagnostic, without scheduling, pacing or transport-timestamp changes. Same nine ascending twenty-second points and retained daemons as v1; no overlapping builds/tests/Git packing.

V2 adds an outgoing-insertion timestamp to each pooled Permit/Complete/Report. Successful foreign pushes add insertion-to-pre-push age; the first timestamp survives failed pushes. Divide queue_ns by enqueued when censoring is zero. Local messages and failed pushes contribute no successful latency samples.

V1 pre-push-to-notify and pre-push-to-consumer measurements are unchanged. The pre-push timestamp precedes publication and can include producer preemption. Mean queue and observation intervals are separately sampled; their sum is not an individually matched message-latency distribution.

Timing uses load-only before/sent snapshots. All retry, censor and pending counts are zero; enqueued equals notified. Consumer count skew reaches 329 messages, 0.137%, across independent snapshots. Raw signed residuals remain; observation minus notification is not direct eventfd wakeup latency.

At 21G, Complete queue means are 11.87/9.41us versus pre-push-to-consumer 11.52/11.02us. Unlimited queue means are 11.98/9.61us. Permit and Report queue means remain below 1us at every point. This measures producer-side completion deferral, not its causal goodput cost.

Goodput varies against v1 and normal release. V2 gives 2.24/2.57G at 4G, 2.75/2.68G at 8G and 2.51/2.64G unlimited. Added clock/counter overhead and run variation prevent a performance-gain claim. An earlier notification experiment on an older sender was inconclusive; a current matched scheduling experiment is still needed.
176 pure tests, 59 ignored library kernel tests, Clippy and formatting passed. The compiled musl clock test made zero clock_gettime syscalls on this host.

All nine points have zero admission pressure, socket overflow/errors, inner UDP errors, malformed/invalid/duplicate/out-of-window/wrong-run/reordered records and outer IPv6 fragmentation. Selective payload repair remains unfinished.

Goodput excludes drain; missing ratios and throughput counter deltas include drain. CPU 100% is one core. ACK-buffer drops are a subset of queue_drops; units differ. Pending-notification gauges are omitted from additive throughput deltas.
